post-fd-newtonian-fourier.physical_scope: An adopted smooth, isotropic, single-component Newtonian/Fourier closure with specified state laws, nonnegative shear and bulk coefficients, and positive-semidefinite symmetric conductivity part. No coefficient is inferred from a measurement and no universal fluid applicability is asserted.

post-fd-newtonian-fourier:
## Postulate

Use a Cartesian inertial frame in Newtonian spacetime. At an event let $u$ be the fluid velocity, $T>0$ its temperature, $\rho>0$ its mass density, and $\xi=(\rho,T)$ its local state in a specified open set $\mathcal S\subset(0,\infty)^2$. The velocity gradient has components $L_{ij}=\partial_{x_j}u_i$; define the symmetric rate matrix $D=(L+L^T)/2$, its trace $\theta=\operatorname{tr}D$, and its trace-free part $D_0=D-\theta I_3/3$, where $I_3$ is the $3\times3$ identity matrix. For $A,B\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}$, use the Frobenius contraction $A:B=\sum_{i,j=1}^3A_{ij}B_{ij}$.

Adopt specified scalar state laws $\mu,\zeta:\mathcal S\to[0,\infty)$ and a specified conductivity matrix law $K:\mathcal S\to\mathbb R^{3\times3}$, with
$$ x^T\operatorname{sym}K(\xi)x\ge0\quad(x\in\mathbb R^3),\qquad \operatorname{sym}K=(K+K^T)/2. $$
Assume the viscous response at a fixed state is linear in $D$ and equivariant under proper rotations, and adopt
$$ \tau=2\mu(\xi)D_0+\zeta(\xi)\theta I_3,\qquad \sigma=-pI_3+\tau,\qquad q=-K(\xi)\nabla T. $$
Here $p$ is the scalar pressure field in the tension-positive convention: the traction on an outward unit normal $n$ is $\sigma n$. Under a rigid observer rotation $Q\in\operatorname{SO}(3)$, the tensor fields transform by $S^*=QSQ^T$; $\mu,\zeta$ are scalar state functions and $K^*=QKQ^T$. The closure is therefore form-invariant under those rotations. The mathematical linear-isotropic classification identifies this stress form from the stated linearity and equivariance hypotheses; it does not establish that any material adopts them.

In SI units, $D,\theta,D_0$ are in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$, $\mu,\zeta$ in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, $K$ in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$, $q$ in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$, and $\sigma,\tau,p$ in $\mathrm{Pa}$. If the same stress is written $2\mu D+\lambda\theta I_3$, then $\lambda=\zeta-2\mu/3$; no nonnegativity of $\lambda$ is assumed. These specified constitutive functions are adopted model inputs, not measured coefficient values or consequences of balance laws.

def-fd-barotropic-euler-model.physical_scope: A smooth unforced inviscid barotropic continuum branch with positive density and a specified C1 pressure law. The pressure law is a model closure; no solution existence, response-sign assumption or empirical applicability is asserted.

def-fd-barotropic-euler-model:
## Definition

Let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be an open time interval, let $\Omega\subset I\times\mathbb R^3$ be open, and let $P:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be a continuously differentiable pressure function. A smooth positive-density barotropic Euler solution is a pair of fields $\rho\in C^2(\Omega,(0,\infty))$ and $u\in C^2(\Omega,\mathbb R^3)$ satisfying
$$ \partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}(\rho u)=0,\qquad \rho\bigl(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u\bigr)+\nabla P(\rho)=0. $$
Here $\operatorname{div}u=\sum_{i=1}^3\partial_{x_i}u_i$, $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient, and $D_tu=\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u$ is the material acceleration. The constitutive stress is $\sigma=-P(\rho)I_3$ under the tension-positive traction convention. Thus “barotropic” means that pressure is a specified function of density alone, and “Euler” here means that the viscous stress is absent. No sign of $P'(\rho)$ is built into the definition; a positive acoustic response is a separate hypothesis where used. In SI interpretation, $\rho$ is in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $u$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $P$ in $\mathrm{Pa}$, and $P'(\rho)$ in $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-2}}$. The model gives equations for a smooth solution and asserts no existence theorem.

def-fd-incompressible-newtonian-model.physical_scope: A smooth, unforced, constant-density incompressible Newtonian branch with a pressure multiplier and constant nonnegative shear viscosity. Boundary and initial data are separate, and no solution existence or empirical applicability is asserted.

def-fd-incompressible-newtonian-model:
## Definition

Let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be an open time interval and $\Omega\subset I\times\mathbb R^3$ open. A smooth constant-density incompressible Newtonian branch has a constant $\rho_0>0$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, a constant dynamic shear viscosity $\mu\ge0$ in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, a velocity field $u\in C^2(\Omega,\mathbb R^3)$, and a pressure multiplier $p\in C^1(\Omega,\mathbb R)$. Define $L_{ij}=\partial_{x_j}u_i$, $D=(L+L^T)/2$, and $D_tu=\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u$. The branch is specified by
$$ \rho=\rho_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}u=0,\qquad \sigma=-pI_3+2\mu D,\qquad \rho_0D_tu=\operatorname{div}\sigma, $$
where $(\operatorname{div}\sigma)_i=\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_{x_j}\sigma_{ij}$. Equivalently, for constant $\mu$, its momentum equation is
$$ \rho_0D_tu+\nabla p=\mu\Delta u,\qquad \Delta u_i=\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_{x_jx_j}u_i. $$
Indeed, $\operatorname{div}(2\mu D)=\mu\Delta u+\mu\nabla(\operatorname{div}u)=\mu\Delta u$. This is the incompressible specialization of the adopted Newtonian closure: $\theta=\operatorname{div}u=0$ implies $D_0=D$, so the bulk-viscosity and Fourier-flux terms do not enter this mechanical equation. The pressure is a constraint multiplier and is not identified with a compressible equation-of-state pressure. Define the kinematic viscosity $\nu=\mu/\rho_0$, in $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$. Boundary and initial data are not part of this definition, and the item asserts no solution existence.

post-fd-local-equilibrium.physical_scope: An adopted local-equilibrium state relation for a smooth single-component simple-fluid branch with positive density and temperature. No global equilibrium, global thermodynamic chart, universal material validity or empirical measurement is asserted.

post-fd-local-equilibrium:
## Postulate

Use a smooth single-component, nonpolar fluid branch in a Cartesian inertial frame. Let $\mathcal U\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ be an open state domain with coordinates $v$ and $s$, where $v$ is specific volume and $s$ is specific entropy. Adopt a specific internal-energy function $e:\mathcal U\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^2$, meaning that its coordinate partial derivatives through total order two exist and are continuous. At a state $(v,s)$, define the temperature and thermodynamic pressure by
$$ T(v,s)=\frac{\partial e}{\partial s}(v,s),\qquad p(v,s)=-\frac{\partial e}{\partial v}(v,s),\qquad \rho=\frac1v, $$
where each partial derivative holds the other state coordinate fixed. Assume the local material states lie in $\mathcal U$ and $T>0$. Local equilibrium here means that the fields $e,T,p$ at each event are assigned by these state functions of the local $v,s$.

In the physical SI interpretation, $v$ is in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}}$, $s$ in $\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$, $e$ in $\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}}$, $T$ in $\mathrm K$, $p$ in $\mathrm{Pa}$, and $\rho$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$. Positivity of $e_{ss}$, global invertibility of $s\mapsto T$, convexity, and the dynamical entropy inequality are separate assumptions or postulates; none follows from this local equilibrium adoption. This closure is an additional physical model choice, not a consequence of global equilibrium thermodynamics.

pthm-fd-entropy-production.physical_scope: Conditional smooth local-equilibrium continuum calculation with positive temperature, the stated local mass and energy-balance hypotheses, and Newtonian/Fourier closure. Entropy production is a pointwise coefficient test, not an empirical validation or a proof of the adopted entropy postulate.

pthm-fd-entropy-production:
## Statement

Assume the complete smooth material, state, contact and mass/momentum/angular-momentum/total-energy balance hypotheses of the local Gibbs-entropy identity, including $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and positive temperature, as stated in Facts & Assumptions. Use a $C^2$ local state relation $e(v,s)$ with $v=1/\rho$, $T=e_s(v,s)>0$, and $p=-e_v(v,s)$. Let $\sigma=-pI_3+\tau$, define $L_{ij}=\partial_{x_j}u_i$, $D=(L+L^T)/2$, $\theta=\operatorname{tr}D$, and set
$$ \mathcal G=\rho D_ts+\operatorname{div}(q/T)-\rho r/T,\qquad D_t=\partial_t+u\cdot\nabla. $$
For the adopted Newtonian/Fourier form $\tau=2\mu D_0+\zeta\theta I_3$, $D_0=D-\theta I_3/3$, and $q=-K\nabla T$, the residual is
$$ \mathcal G=\frac{2\mu|D_0|^2+\zeta\theta^2}{T} +\frac{(\nabla T)^T\operatorname{sym}(K)\nabla T}{T^2}. $$
At a fixed state, if the algebraic coefficient family is tested for every symmetric $D$, every $g=\nabla T\in\mathbb R^3$, and every $T>0$, this residual is nonnegative exactly when $\mu\ge0$, $\zeta\ge0$, and $x^T\operatorname{sym}(K)x\ge0$ for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$. These conditions make the adopted closure compatible with the separate continuum entropy inequality. The theorem does not derive the balance or entropy postulates, infer material coefficients, or assert empirical validity.

pthm-fd-acoustic-linearization.physical_scope: First variation about a uniform rest state of the adopted smooth, positive-density barotropic model when its pressure law is the fixed-entropy restriction of the adopted local state relation. The prediction is linear; no finite-amplitude error, lifespan, material measurement or empirical sound-speed claim is asserted.

pthm-fd-acoustic-linearization:
## Statement

Let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open time interval and $\Omega\subset I\times\mathbb R^3$ a nonempty open domain for the model fields. Let $e\in C^2(\mathcal U)$ be the local specific-energy relation on an open $\mathcal U\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, with state coordinates $(v,s)$, $T=e_s$, and $p=-e_v$; each state partial derivative holds the other coordinate fixed. Fix $(v_b,s_b)\in\mathcal U$ with $T_b>0$ and $e_{ss}(v_b,s_b)>0$, set $\rho_b=1/v_b$, and take the barotropic pressure law to be $P(\rho)=p(1/\rho,s_b)$ near $\rho_b$. This is the fixed-entropy restriction of the adopted local state relation. The smooth barotropic Euler model is linearized about the uniform rest state $(\rho,u)=(\rho_b,0)$. For $C^2$ perturbation fields $\delta\rho:I\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ and $w:I\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$, the first variation at $\varepsilon=0$ after $\rho=\rho_b+\varepsilon\delta\rho$, $u=\varepsilon w$ is
$$ \partial_t\delta\rho+\rho_b\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad \rho_b\partial_tw+P'(\rho_b)\nabla\delta\rho=0,\qquad \partial_{tt}\delta\rho=c_s^2\Delta\delta\rho, \quad c_s^2=P'(\rho_b)=v_b^2e_{vv}(v_b,s_b). $$
The sign of $c_s^2$ is not assumed in the base model. If $c_s^2>0$, define $c_s=\sqrt{c_s^2}$. For every nonzero $k\in\mathbb R^3$, with $\omega=c_s|k|$, the fields
$$ \delta\rho=A\cos(k\cdot x-\omega t),\qquad w=\frac{\omega A}{\rho_b|k|^2}k\cos(k\cdot x-\omega t) $$
solve the first-variation system for every real amplitude $A$. They are exact solutions of the linearized equations, not finite-amplitude approximations with an automatic error or lifespan bound. No empirical value of $c_s$ is asserted.

pthm-fd-perfect-gas-temperature.physical_scope: Conditional smooth local-equilibrium calculation for an explicitly adopted calorically perfect gas with positive specific gas constant and specific heat. The temperature equation includes stress, heat flux and heat supply; entropy constancy and the isentropic pressure law are restricted to the stated adiabatic, inviscid, unsourced branch. No empirical gas data or universal gas model is asserted.

pthm-fd-perfect-gas-temperature:
## Statement

Assume the complete smooth material, state, contact and mass/momentum/angular-momentum/total-energy balance hypotheses of the mathematical Gibbs-entropy identity, including $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, as stated in Facts & Assumptions. Let $R>0$ be a specific gas constant and $c_v>0$ a constant specific heat at constant volume, both in $\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$. Choose reference values $T_{\mathrm{ref}}>0$ in $\mathrm K$, $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}>0$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, and $s_{\mathrm{ref}}$ in $\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$. On $v>0,\ s\in\mathbb R$, adopt
$$ T(v,s)=T_{\mathrm{ref}}\exp\!\left(\frac{s-s_{\mathrm{ref}}}{c_v}\right) \left(\frac{1}{\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}v}\right)^{R/c_v},\qquad e(v,s)=c_vT(v,s),\qquad p(v,s)=\frac{R\,T(v,s)}{v}. $$
These formulas give $T=e_s>0$, $p=-e_v$, and $e\in C^2((0,\infty)\times\mathbb R)$; equivalently, with $\rho=1/v$, $s=s_{\mathrm{ref}}+c_v\ln(T/T_{\mathrm{ref}})-R\ln(\rho/\rho_{\mathrm{ref}})$ and $p=\rho RT$. The logarithms have dimensionless arguments.

For a smooth solution, define $\theta=\operatorname{div}u$, $\sigma=-pI_3+\tau$, and the local entropy residual $\mathcal G=\rho D_ts+\operatorname{div}(q/T)-\rho r/T$. The temperature balance is
$$ \rho c_vD_tT=-p\theta+\tau:D-\operatorname{div}q+\rho r. $$
On the additional adiabatic, inviscid, unsourced branch $\tau=0,\ q=0,\ r=0$, one has $D_ts=0$. Along any trajectory on which the entropy value is $s_0$, the pressure law is
$$ p=K(s_0)\rho^\gamma,\qquad \gamma=1+\frac{R}{c_v},\qquad K(s_0)=RT_{\mathrm{ref}}\exp\!\left(\frac{s_0-s_{\mathrm{ref}}}{c_v}\right) \rho_{\mathrm{ref}}^{-R/c_v}>0. $$
The factor $K(s_0)$ can differ between trajectories with different entropy values. The gas closure is an adopted model, and the adiabatic conclusion does not apply when viscous work, heat conduction, or heat supply is present.

pthm-fd-newtonian-kinetic-decay.physical_scope: Conditional kinetic-energy identity for an actual smooth unforced, constant-density incompressible Newtonian solution on a fixed no-slip domain or periodic domain. It asserts no existence, uniqueness, long-time regularity, global solution or empirical realization.

pthm-fd-newtonian-kinetic-decay:
## Statement

Let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open time interval containing $0$. Suppose a smooth solution of the constant-density incompressible Newtonian model has $\rho=\rho_0>0$, $\operatorname{div}u=0$, constant $\mu\ge0$, zero body force, and stress $\sigma=-pI_3+2\mu D$. Assume the complete $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, smooth-motion, positive-density, contact/stress-regularity, continuity, and separate linear/angular-momentum and total-energy balance hypotheses of the mathematical local-balance equivalence result, as specified in Facts & Assumptions. The spatial region is either a nonempty bounded $C^1$ domain fixed in time with no-slip condition $u=0$ on its boundary, or a periodic domain with the fields and their derivatives periodic on opposite faces of a rectangular period cell with positive side lengths. For the periodic case, interpret the local balance assumptions on the periodic lift to $\mathbb R^3$.

For $D=(\nabla u+\nabla u^T)/2$, let $E_k(t)=\frac{\rho_0}{2}\int_\Omega |u(t,x)|^2\,dx$, using one period cell in the periodic case. For every $t_1<t_2$ in $I$,
$$ E_k(t_2)+2\mu\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\int_\Omega |D(t,x)|^2\,dx\,dt=E_k(t_1). $$
Thus $E_k$ is nonincreasing; strict decay is not claimed when $D$ vanishes. The theorem is conditional on an actual smooth solution and supplies no existence or long-time regularity result.

cex-fd-negative-bulk-viscosity.physical_scope: Algebraic counterexample in the Newtonian/Fourier residual family with negative bulk coefficient. This coefficient lies outside the adopted nonnegative-bulk postulate; the example is not a material observation or claim about a realized fluid.

cex-fd-negative-response-acoustics.physical_scope: Exact counterexample for the linearized equations of an explicitly adopted smooth barotropic state relation with negative fixed-entropy pressure response. It is not a finite-amplitude solution or an empirical claim about a realized material.
